title: heap overflow in statDecodePage; needs -DSQLITE_ENABLE_DBSTAT_VTAB
live_proof: fuzz-corpus diff: the image reproduces on stock 3.22.0 under host ASan as a SEGV / out-of-bounds read in statDecodePage at sqlite3.c:177956
arena_bytes_why: 1 MiB on every arm. Five of the eight spatial cases are forced here by reachability -- at 262144 cases 21, 22 and 23 exhaust memsys5 before the defect (pcache1AllocPage dereferences the NULL that 3.22.0 does not check), 29 returns SQLITE_NOMEM, and 00 takes a different path -- so the same value is declared for all eight to keep the arms comparable. Measured 2026-10-17; this is also the value every recorded virtual reading was taken at, while CheriBSD had been running 262144.
object: the page buffer statDecodePage walks while reporting dbstat rows: the cell-pointer walk at iOff += getVarint32(&aData[iOff], nPayload). Measured 2026-10-16 by probe site 64, which hooks all three unchecked reads in that function and shows this case taking the cell walk with iOff reaching 64768, the free-block chain never running, and the witness reporting kind=CAP-OOB with ca past the arena's own end
lifetime_ender: not a lifetime defect: a corrupt page makes the cell-pointer walk leave the buffer
shape: read past the end of the record
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator, with a reconstructed trigger (see case 24, which explains why the SQL for these R2 images had to be re-derived; the old text said case 34, a number from the 38-case corpus that no longer exists). Needs -DSQLITE_ENABLE_DBSTAT_VTAB, without which the statement fails with 'no such table: dbstat' and the case passes having tested nothing

status: re-measured on all four readings 2026-10-16 on this platform. host ASan was re-run on a restored x86 runtime: heap-buffer-overflow in statDecodePage at the cell-pointer walk, via statNext <- statFilter, identical to the 2026-10-11 bundle. virtual-malloc MISSED, RETURNED, both controls as declared -- against the physical spatial row, which reports cause 5 load out of bounds; the two builds disagree, as in case 24. virtual-nested-pools CAUGHT, cause=28 pc=0x3fa6212aa4 in statDecodePage, both controls as declared. cheribsd-revocation CAUGHT: SIGPROT(34) si_code=1 PROT_CHERI_BOUNDS, pc=0x1ca032 resolving to statDecodePage+828, with the image loaded (s0_rc=11) and the boot positive control trapping. THE CHERIBSD READING CHANGES, AND NOT BECAUSE OF THE MECHANISM. The nine spatial cases were all recorded not-detected on 2026-10-06, and those readings were taken without their corrupt database images present -- the silent failure found while reviewing case 21 and fixed in e9199203, where sqlite3_open creates an empty database, the first statement returns 'no such table' and the case prints RETURNED rc=0. With the images restored on 2026-10-16, on the same binaries and the same arm, this case faults. The 10-06 TSV records it as PASS. The arms block is the 2026-10-11 bundle's and is regenerated by derive-verdicts.py when this review ends. RE-MEASURED 2026-10-17 with one arena on every arm (arena_bytes=1048576) and every arm built from the corpus case.c: virtual-malloc MISSED, virtual-nested-pools CAUGHT cause=28 pc=0x3f95a12aa4 in statDecodePage, cheribsd-revocation MISSED with RETURNED rc=0 and probe site 64 reporting hits=9 witnesses=7 -- reached and silent, not a no-reading. The earlier spatial readings were taken with the virtual arms at a 1 MiB header default against CheriBSD's 262144, and with this arm compiling its own copy of the case
note: Re-measured 2026-10-16; the CheriBSD cell goes from MISSED to CAUGHT and everything else holds. The reason is the one in status -- the 2026-10-06 reading was taken without the corrupt image -- and the new fault is a bounds violation on a VALID capability (si_code=1, PROT_CHERI_BOUNDS), resolving into statDecodePage, the declared site, where the Sublet arm also faults with cause 28. Probe site 64 gives the mechanism directly: this case takes the cell-pointer walk, iOff reaching 64768 in eight iterations, and the witness reports kind=CAP-OOB with cb=<arena>+262144 and ca=0x21d120, which is past the arena's own end. That is why a mechanism with malloc-granularity bounds can see this case: the over-read leaves the whole 256 KiB arena. The other spatial cases whose over-reads stay inside it are invisible there, which is the distinction the arm's column now rests on. The free-block chain never runs on this image, which is what separates this case from 32; probe site 64 hooks all three unchecked reads in statDecodePage and the three images split cleanly -- 31 the cell walk, 32 the chain, 29 both with its own sqlite3Get4byte read on top. The two base builds disagree here as in case 24: the physical row reports cause 5 and the virtual-malloc build completes, which is build-dependence in where the over-read lands relative to the arena end, not a difference in what the mechanism can check
fault_sites_why: Host ASan, running the same case source on stock 3.22.0, reports the invalid access in statDecodePage (live_proof); that run is independent of the Capstone arms and predates them.
